docs.t: Judge Loretta Preska (S.D.N.Y.) — Joint pretrial order
docs.x: Judge Loretta Preska, S.D.N.Y.. Joint pretrial order: Due within 30 days after the discovery completion date unless otherwise ordered. Include the caption; trial counsel’s contact information; jurisdiction statements with statutes and citizenship and amount facts; each party’s claims and defenses to be tried (and those not to be tried); jury or nonjury and trial days; whether all parties consent to a magistrate judge (without saying who); stipulations; witness lists (live or by deposition); deposition designations with counter-designations and objections; and exhibit lists, marking with one star exhibits unobjected to on authenticity and two stars exhibits unobjected to on any ground.

docs.t: Judge Loretta Preska (S.D.N.Y.) — Pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Loretta Preska, S.D.N.Y.. Pretrial filings: Due 15 days before trial if a date is set, or 30 days after the final pretrial order is filed if not: in jury cases, requests to charge and proposed voir dire (jury charges also sent electronically to the law clerk when feasible); in non-jury cases, a statement of the elements of each claim or defense with a summary of supporting facts; in all cases, motions in limine; and an optional pretrial memorandum. Submit General Purpose Computing Device Orders to chambers at least 5 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Loretta Preska (S.D.N.Y.) — Sentencing
docs.x: Judge Loretta Preska, S.D.N.Y.. Sentencing: Defendant’s submission is served 2 weeks before sentencing and the government’s 1 week before, and each is filed publicly when served, with all letters grouped under one cover (paper) or as attachments to one document (ECF) marked SENTENCING MEMORANDUM. The defense files letters on the defendant’s behalf; the government files victims’ letters. The five sensitive and six caution categories in the Privacy Policy may be redacted without leave; only redacted pages are filed under seal, with a copy sent to chambers and another handed up at sentencing marked to show the redactions. Redactions beyond those eleven categories require an application served and filed with the submission. The Individual Practices do not override statutory or rule-based deadlines, such as those under Fed. R. Civ. P. 50, 52, 54, 59, and 60 and Fed. R. App. P. 4.

docs.x: Judge Jed S. Rakoff, S.D.N.Y.. Settlement: No adjournment for settlement without a stipulation or letter from all parties affirming final settlement and consenting to dismissal with prejudice. Absent good cause, the stipulation may not allow reopening, or retention of jurisdiction (except to enforce injunctive relief), beyond 30 days after dismissal.

docs.t: Judge Jed S. Rakoff (S.D.N.Y.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Jed S. Rakoff, S.D.N.Y.. Criminal cases: Brady material known at indictment (other than Giglio) must be produced within 2 weeks of indictment, even during plea talks; later-learned Brady material within 2 weeks of learning it and at least 4 weeks before trial or plea; Giglio material 4 weeks before trial or plea. Sentencing is normally within 90 days of plea or verdict (cooperators: a date proposed at plea, never more than 3 years out). docs.t: Judge Jed S. Rakoff (S.D.N.Y.) — Electronic devices

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — Pre-motion letter
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. Pre-motion letter: Before a motion to dismiss, for a more definite statement, to remand, to change venue, to compel arbitration, or for judgment on the pleadings in a civil case, send a three-page letter including your signature requesting a conference. Adversaries answer in three pages within seven days, with no reply unless directed. The court may order you to meet and confer first. Only issues in the letters are discussed. It doesn’t waive jurisdiction or service defenses and tolls your time, with seven extra days if the court skips the conference. It doesn’t apply to pro se cases, bankruptcy, or Social Security appeals.

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. Motions generally: Follow L.Civ.R. 7.1 and 7.2 strictly. Overlength requests are highly disfavored. PDFs must be text searchable at a minimum 400 dpi or may be rejected. Short extensions of two weeks or less that don’t affect other dates are generally granted if everyone agrees. Longer ones for trial, discovery cutoff, or dispositive motions need compelling reasons made well ahead. No sur-reply without permission, and if allowed, due in seven days and no more than ten pages.

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. Summary judgment: A summary judgment motion without a Rule 56.1 statement is dismissed. The judge won’t consider facts without pinpoint cites. The responsive statement must repeat each fact and say agreed or disagreed with cites, or the fact is treated as undisputed. The statements can’t contain legal argument or evidentiary objections. The judge prefers the old Appendix N bundling approach: serve the motion, opposition, and reply, then file them all together in order when briefing is done, with an index of where each exhibit is docketed. Ask the magistrate judge for a conference promptly about a noncompliant statement, and raise any expert exclusion plans first.

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — Emergent relief
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. Emergent relief: Detail your efforts to resolve the issue with the other side and serve the papers on them, absent a true emergency. Proposed findings and conclusions will be required for TRO and injunction hearings.

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — Trial submissions
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. Trial submissions: One week before trial submit a joint exhibit list in hard copy and Word, with columns for the exhibit, the opponent’s objection, and the proponent’s basis for admissibility, plus three bench books of exhibits. Also submit a combined neutral statement of the case, combined preliminary and final jury instructions and verdict sheet with disagreements in two columns, with double-spaced instructions and footnoted authority, tracking model charges and marking changes, and combined voir dire questions. The judge conducts voir dire from a script counsel can review and holds a housekeeping meeting before jury selection.

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — In the courtroom
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. In the courtroom: The judge disfavors speaking objections, doesn’t allow juror notes or questions, prefers peremptories announced standing with one pass, and usually charges before closings. Trial runs Monday through Thursday, 9:30 to 3:30, so one lawyer per party examines each witness. Be within 10 minutes of the courthouse during deliberations. Cell phones and cameras are prohibited and may be confiscated.

docs.t: Judge Evelyn Padin (D.N.J.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Evelyn Padin, D.N.J.. Criminal cases: Procedures are generally the same. File everything on CM/ECF, and plea documents go to chambers two weeks before the plea. Sentencing memoranda go directly to the court with a Submission Notice, due two weeks before sentencing for moving submissions and one week for responses, with a process for public requests and redactions.

docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Conferral: The order takes precedence over conflicting local procedures. You must actually speak, in person, by phone, or by Zoom, since email alone isn’t enough, and the motion must include a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery motion
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Discovery motion: File a discovery motion of no more than five pages that frames the issues, cites the best authority, and attaches the relevant requests and responses, described under CM/ECF procedure 3L(2). The response is due in five business days in five pages, and no reply is allowed. The judge then decides on a hearing. The parties may agree to extend interim discovery deadlines, such as response dates, without the court as long as the discovery cutoff and other scheduling order dates don’t change. The judge won’t take calls or attempts to get immediate rulings on deposition conduct, so proceed with the deposition and raise it by post-deposition motion. Keep trying to resolve it after a hearing is set and tell chambers promptly.

docs.t: Judge Ryon M. McCabe (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Ryon M. McCabe, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No boilerplate or general objections, and vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless. Explain specifically and support burden with an affidavit. Ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness, say whether a request is irrelevant or disproportionate and why, confer to narrow scope, and produce the undisputed part. An objection followed by an answer subject to it preserves nothing. Privilege objections must follow Local Rule 26.1(e)(2)(B) and include a log, or may be waived.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Motion for Hearing and source materials
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Motion for Hearing and source materials: On the day the judge confirms your time, file a Motion for Hearing stating the date, the category of the discovery issues, the status of your pre-filing efforts, and a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate of conferral, or it can be denied. By noon on the Monday before the hearing, give the judge the source materials by hand or as a scanned PDF to the chambers mailbox, with a proposed order stating the specific relief for each request. Missing any of the three may cancel the hearing. Tell the judge promptly if you resolve or narrow the dispute. After the hearing, file a motion for entry of an amended proposed order within two business days.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral and timing
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Conferral and timing: You must actually confer, and an adequate certificate almost always needs at least one personal communication, since unanswered emails aren’t enough. The judge deems an issue waived if you don’t confer or certify. Judge Torres strictly enforces Local Rule 26.1(g)(2), reads the 28-day window as the time to make resolution efforts with only the seven-day agreed extension, and doesn’t recognize unapproved extensions. All discovery, including resolving disputes, must be done by the cutoff and the judge gives no remedy after it.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Privilege and burden
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Privilege and burden: The party with the burden on a privilege claim must present sworn evidence by the hearing, or the privilege may be deemed waived, and the evidence goes in the emailed materials and on the docket as a notice of filing. The objecting party carries the burden of showing specifically how a request is unreasonable, and failing that brings an order compelling and possible sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No conclusory boilerplate objections, and vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless, and burden may need sworn evidence. Relevance objections must explain why. Don’t recite an objection and then answer subject to it, which preserves nothing, and state that everything responsive was provided or describe what is withheld. Generalized privilege objections don’t comply with Local Rule 26.1(e)(2)(B). Object to a Rule 30(b)(6) notice’s scope by serving, not filing, the objections, and the judge decides them only after the deposition.

docs.t: Judge Edwin G. Torres (S.D. Fla.) — Depositions and sequencing
docs.x: Judge Edwin G. Torres, S.D. Fla.. Depositions and sequencing: To object to deposition timing, serve a notice of objection within five days after receiving the notice, not on the eve, or the objection may be waived, then confer and use the discovery calendar if you can’t agree. Each party may sequence its own discovery under Rule 26(d)(3), and don’t wait until the end to take depositions, since failing to finish them isn’t good cause to extend discovery. The judge strictly enforces Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures and will compel supplemental depositions if they weren’t followed.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Applicable rules and unaccepted filings
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Applicable rules and unaccepted filings: The judge’s Court Practices and Procedures for Civil Cases (last updated June 5, 2019) sits on top of the Federal and Local Rules. The court won’t accept notices of unavailability, notices of deposition, or other filings the rules don’t contemplate, and will strike them. A notice of unavailability doesn’t change the schedule.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Proposed orders: Email a Word version of every proposed order to chambers, as Local Rule 7.1(a)(2) requires. Proposed scheduling orders must follow the judge’s sample format and be emailed after they are filed.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Extensions: Deadlines are strict. Move for an extension at least 48 hours before the deadline unless there is an emergency, or risk sanctions. The motion must list prior extension motions and rulings, state the circumstances, include the Local Rule 7.1 conferral statement, and request a specific period. Indefinite requests are denied, and after a scheduling order extensions are disfavored.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Summary judgment: Follow Local Rule 56.1. The movant files a numbered statement of undisputed facts with record cites, and the opponent answers by corresponding number, saying disputed or undisputed and why a dispute is material. Facts the evidence supports are deemed admitted unless controverted.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Excess pages and sealing
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Excess pages and sealing: A motion for excess pages must say how many pages and why. A motion to seal must state the period to seal, indefinite sealing needs a substantial showing, and a proposed redacted version must accompany it and be filed publicly if the motion is granted.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Motions in limine: Each side may file one motion in limine, with up to ten numbered evidentiary issues, in no more than 20 pages. Confer on every issue first and certify it under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3), and raise only issues still contested. Responses and replies follow the movant’s order and numbering.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Pretrial filings: Use the judge’s witness list and exhibit list formats, list only witnesses you will actually call with a short synopsis, related exhibits, and time estimates, and tie each exhibit to a witness. Joint proposed jury instructions follow the Eleventh Circuit pattern, with plaintiff’s language underlined and defendant’s italicized, authority for every instruction, and emailed in Word. Joint deposition designations use color highlighting, with objections underlined in red and the basis in the margin.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Settlement: Tell the court immediately by call or email and file a joint stipulation of dismissal promptly. The court won’t retain jurisdiction over confidential settlements unless the terms are put on the record, and then only for a finite period.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen M. Williams (S.D. Fla.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge Kathleen M. Williams, S.D. Fla.. Communications with chambers: Requests for relief go on the docket as motions. No substantive matters by phone or email, and no calls about anything the rules or docket answer. Letters aren’t accepted, and ex parte letters are put on the docket. Email subject lines must show the docket number, caption, and contents, and copy all counsel. Calls come only from counsel of record after conferring with all parties, with opposing counsel on the line, giving the docket number, caption, name, whether opposing counsel was consulted, and the reason.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Proposed orders: Email the final Word version of proposed orders and jury instructions to chambers under CM/ECF Administrative Procedure 3.I(6), with the case number and a short description in the subject line, copying all counsel.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Status report and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Status report and scheduling: The Notice of Status Conference requires a Joint Status Report, which satisfies Rule 16. After the status conference the court enters a scheduling order. Calendar every date.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Extensions: Motions to extend, continue, or enlarge are rarely granted. Each party gets one, and no second request after a grant. The caption must show the motions deadline, pretrial conference, calendar call, trial period, the number of prior extension requests, and whether the motion is referred to the magistrate judge, or it is summarily denied. Ask to extend discovery at least 10 days before the deadline, and the court generally won’t allow discovery past it, without changing other deadlines.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Form and conferral
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Form and conferral: Papers are one-sided, double-spaced, 12-point, with one-inch margins and page numbers at the bottom. Every motion needs a proposed order emailed separately in Word or WordPerfect with the docket entry in the subject line. State the other side’s position and describe your conferral efforts with dates under Local Rule 7.1.a.3, or expect denial.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Trial and mediation
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Trial and mediation: Be ready for the scheduled trial, because over 90 percent of cases are reached in the trial period. In consent cases put “CONSENT CASE” in bold under the case number. Use mediation early, and ask for a settlement conference before the magistrate judge at any time.

docs.t: Judge Donald L. Graham (S.D. Fla.) — Pending motions
docs.x: Judge Donald L. Graham, S.D. Fla.. Pending motions: If a ripe motion, or a decision after oral argument or a bench trial, is pending more than 45 days, contact chambers and tell the Judicial Administrator.

docs.t: Judge Paul Huck (S.D. Fla.) — What the page is
docs.x: Judge Paul Huck, S.D. Fla.. What the page is: It is a long “Friendly Random Advice for Litigants” guide, not a set of rules. It says to read the Local Rules and not to surprise the judge.

docs.t: Judge Paul Huck (S.D. Fla.) — Motions practice
docs.x: Judge Paul Huck, S.D. Fla.. Motions practice: Raise problems with opposing counsel and then the court as early as possible. State the issue and relief up front. Be brief, avoid acronyms, and use names, not pronouns. File summary judgment motions early, not at the deadline. Local Rule 7.1.C.2 bars multiple summary judgment motions, so get approval first for a successive one. File a reply or tell the court you won’t, or the court waits for the reply deadline and may take your silence as conceding points. Don’t adopt other filings by reference, and cite the record by page and line.

docs.t: Judge Paul Huck (S.D. Fla.) — Record and logistics
docs.x: Judge Paul Huck, S.D. Fla.. Record and logistics: Ask chambers whether the judge wants mini-script depositions or a separate courtesy set. Keep the record lean, and get approval before exceeding length limits. Test equipment for virtual hearings. Call chambers as soon as an issue is resolved or the case settles. Be careful with emergency motions, and never file one at 4:45 p.m. on a Friday.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Only counsel of record may contact chambers, and absent a true emergency not about the status of pending matters. Use of electronic devices in the judge’s hearings requires a motion.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — CM/ECF
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. CM/ECF: If personal information is filed by mistake, move to strike and file a redacted version. Non-trial exhibits may be attachments but must be labeled by content, not just a number or letter, and documents with several attachments need PDF bookmarks. Proposed orders go in as an attachment and by email in an editable format, preferably Word.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Civil practice
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Civil practice: The judge generally issues a standard pretrial scheduling order and holds pretrial conferences, Daubert hearings (the challenged expert must attend), and motions in limine hearings. Judge Hunt has no extra rules for extensions, continuances, or ex parte restraining orders. The judge hears preliminary injunction motions and takes evidence. Telephone hearings and oral argument are allowed on advance request for good cause. Don’t send copies of published cases.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery and settlement
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Discovery and settlement: The judge generally issues an order setting discovery deadlines and procedures. Don’t call chambers for an immediate ruling during a deposition. Mediation is required in all cases, and counsel submit a proposed referral order. Tell chambers immediately of a settlement and file a notice.

docs.t: Judge Patrick M. Hunt (S.D. Fla.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Patrick M. Hunt, S.D. Fla.. Trial: The judge sets trial dates after conferring with lead counsel and requires trial briefs in bench trials. Counsel conduct voir dire, peremptory strikes alternate, and back striking isn’t allowed. Judge Hunt may limit opening statements, requires advance approval for demonstratives in them, and bars plaintiff rebuttal in openings. No speaking objections. Proposed jury instructions go in electronically, and in bench trials proposed findings are filed electronically.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Chambers: Email proposed orders, jury instructions, and other filings the court directs to the chambers address, and copy all counsel and pro se parties except on confidential statements. The judge’s page also gives telephonic hearing dial-in instructions.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Protective orders
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Protective orders: A stipulation to keep discovery confidential isn’t a court order. File a joint motion for a Rule 26(c) protective order and send the proposed order in Word to chambers. The judge omits any provision that would bypass Local Rule 5.4’s sealing requirements.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No boilerplate objections. Say specifically how a request is vague, overbroad, unduly burdensome, irrelevant, or disproportionate, and ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness. “Not reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence” is outdated. If you object to scope, produce what isn’t disputed. State what you’re withholding. Providing discovery “subject to and without waiving” an objection is improper and the objection is waived. Blanket privilege objections need a privilege log or may be deemed waived, and production of nonprivileged material can’t wait for the log. Object to a Rule 30(b)(6) notice’s scope by serving objections before the deposition, not by moving for a protective order. The objector carries the burden, and failure shifts fees under Rule 37.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Timing and conferral
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Timing and conferral: Raise discovery disputes within Local Rule 26.1(g)(2)’s time, which the judge strictly enforces. All discovery, including resolving disputes, must be done by the cutoff, and the judge offers no remedy after it, even by agreement. Before raising a dispute, confer by live conversation, since email alone isn’t enough, and certify the dates and means under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3). Failing to confer can alone justify denial, and the other side’s failure counts against it on fees.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Two ways to raise a dispute
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Two ways to raise a dispute: You may file a written discovery motion without leave, limited to ten pages for the motion and response and five for a reply, and a hearing isn’t guaranteed. Or use the judge’s Informal Discovery Hearing procedure, which isn’t mandatory and can’t decide sanctions motions but can decide a Rule 37(a) motion to compel.

docs.t: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis (S.D. Fla.) — Informal discovery hearing
docs.x: Judge Lauren Fleischer Louis, S.D. Fla.. Informal discovery hearing: Confer and identify at least two dates within the next 14 days. The movant sends one email to chambers copying all parties, with the subject “Request for Discovery Hearing,” the case number and caption, the proposed dates, the expected length, and a certification of conferral. After the judge confirms, file a Notice of Hearing within 24 hours (two business days for a pro se movant) describing each dispute in two or three sentences without argument, or it is stricken. By noon two business days before, each party emails the relevant source materials, separately and with descriptive titles, and a proposed order stating the specific relief for each request.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Communication
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Communication: Law clerks can answer procedural questions, not substantive or strategy questions. Have the case number and presiding judge ready. Absent a true emergency, counsel of record shouldn’t ask about the status of pending matters. Telephonic hearing dial-in instructions are on the judge’s page.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Electronic equipment
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Electronic equipment: To bring audio or video equipment into the courtroom, comply with Administrative Order 2018-79 and file the motion at least 48 hours ahead. The judge posts a sample order.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Discovery: Judge Reinhart is guided by the Standing Discovery Order, the Florida Bar guidelines for professional conduct, and the Chief Justice’s 2015 Year-End Report. The judge’s page also posts an Order Setting Discovery Status Conference, the judge’s best-practices article, a discovery remedies chart, Rule 502(d) clawback order forms, and confidentiality order forms.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: Ordinarily only one lawyer per party may argue. If a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, tell the court before the hearing starts and multiple lawyers may argue for that party.

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Standing Discovery Order (January 2024)
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Standing Discovery Order (January 2024): The order applies to discovery in the judge’s cases and sanctions can follow noncompliance. Relevance and proportionality objections need a specific explanation. Responding doesn’t waive objections to future requests. If parties can’t agree on a deposition date after conferring, the requesting party may set it with Local Rule 26.1(h) notice and the deponent must move for a protective order. The judge won’t rule on ESI search disputes in advance: the responding party searches and the requester can challenge whether the inquiry was reasonable. Instructions that impose duties beyond the rules have no effect. A response promising production at an indeterminate time is unacceptable, so give a completion date, and a final production date more than 30 days after the response deadline is presumptively unreasonable. A pr

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery objections
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Discovery objections: No boilerplate or general objections, and the court strikes them. Say whether responsive material is being withheld, and a later claim that no documents exist after an objection draws sanctions. Ask for clarification before objecting that a term is vague, and otherwise define the term yourself and respond. Overbroad is ambiguous, so say whether you mean irrelevant or disproportionate. Confer to narrow scope, and answer the undisputed part. “Subject to and without waiving” objections are barred, and for interrogatories an objection plus an answer waives the objection. “To the extent that” objections are inadequate. Privilege objections need the specifics and a log, or they may be waived. Privilege at a deposition is raised question by question. For a Rule 30(b)(6) notice the judge typically won’t rule on objections in advance, and

docs.t: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Bruce E. Reinhart, S.D. Fla.. Discovery disputes: You must actually speak with opposing counsel, in person or by phone. Don’t file a discovery motion first. The movant emails chambers with the subject “Request for Discovery Hearing,” offering two afternoons within the next seven business days, the time needed, and a certification of conferral, copying all counsel. The judge sets the hearing by order and counsel appear in person. At least 48 hours before, file a joint discovery memorandum of five pages or less describing the dispute, certifying conferral, and attaching the source materials, in the judge’s sample format. If it isn’t resolved Judge Reinhart may authorize a motion, which then triggers Rule 37(a)(5) fees.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Objections: An objection that a request isn’t reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence is outdated and meritless on its own. Relevance and proportionality objections need a specific explanation. No generalized, vague, or boilerplate objections. “Vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome” alone is meaningless and stricken. Ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness. “Overbroad” alone is inadequate, so say whether you mean irrelevant or disproportionate and why. Confer to narrow scope, answer the undisputed part, and support a burden claim with an affidavit. Unless impractical, support a burden objection to ESI search terms with evidence of the expected number of hits.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral and timing
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Conferral and timing: Counsel must actually speak, in person or by phone. Email or text isn’t enough, and you should discuss every request and objection at issue. Seek court help within 28 days of when the grounds arise under Local Rule 26.1(g)(2)(A), and at least seven days before the discovery cutoff absent exceptional circumstances, or the relief can be denied automatically. Conferring before objections doesn’t excuse conferring again before requesting a hearing.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — No written discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. No written discovery motions: Don’t file written discovery motions between parties unless an order authorizes it. This covers any Rule 26 or Rule 37 motion, including to compel, for a protective order, for discovery sanctions, to strike an untimely expert, and to extend time to respond to discovery, though the judge expects you to agree to reasonable extensions. The exception is a dispute with a non-party, which can be raised by motion of five double-spaced pages with no reply, and you must give the non-party a copy of the judge’s procedures.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Notice of Discovery Dispute
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Notice of Discovery Dispute: To get a hearing, file a Notice of Discovery Dispute, not a motion, after conferring on every issue. It describes the dispute in one or two sentences, states the discovery deadline and your conferral efforts, offers at least three alternative dates within two weeks with morning, afternoon, or all-day availability, gives the time needed, and certifies conferral. No argument, and the opposing party doesn’t respond. If the other side completely failed to respond by a firm deadline, file a Notice of Complete Failure to Respond to Discovery with three dates, and the judge cancels the hearing if the discovery is produced.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Joint discovery status report
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Joint discovery status report: At least 48 hours before the hearing, file a joint report and email a Word copy. For each dispute, give the verbatim request and response, a succinct statement of each side’s position, and the result of conferral, in the judge’s chart, with the combined positions on one page per request. Keep trying to resolve or narrow the dispute and tell chambers promptly if you do.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Fees and hearings
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Fees and hearings: The judge treats arguments at the hearing as oral motions to compel or for a protective order and requires the loser to pay fees under Rule 37(a)(5) where warranted, and may impose other sanctions. Ordinarily one lawyer per party argues, but if a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, tell the judge beforehand and multiple lawyers may argue.

docs.t: Judge Jared M. Strauss (S.D. Fla.) — Stipulated orders
docs.x: Judge Jared M. Strauss, S.D. Fla.. Stipulated orders: File a joint motion attaching the proposed order, then immediately email a Word copy to the chambers address.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Communication and equipment
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Communication and equipment: Law clerks can answer procedural questions only. Have the case number and presiding judge ready. Absent a true emergency, counsel of record shouldn’t ask about the status of pending matters. Motions to bring electronic equipment into court are due at least 72 hours before the hearing or trial, under Administrative Order 2018-79.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Arguing lawyers
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Arguing lawyers: Ordinarily one attorney per party argues, but if you tell the court before the hearing that a lawyer with five or fewer years’ experience will argue, multiple attorneys may.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Conferral: Counsel must actually speak, in person, by phone, or by video. Email or a voicemail alone isn’t enough. Keep trying after a hearing is set, and tell chambers promptly if issues resolve.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Scheduling a hearing
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Scheduling a hearing: After conferring, call chambers to get available dates, confirm them with opposing counsel, and call back to finalize. Make multiple attempts to reach opposing counsel, and if there is no response in three business days you may finalize a date that fits your own schedule. Continuing that hearing then takes a motion showing good cause with three alternative dates. The first discovery hearing is typically by Zoom unless you request otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery motion
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Discovery motion: The same day you finalize the hearing, file a concise discovery motion of no more than three pages, with the specific substance, the best authority, a conferral certification, and the source materials attached. Only one per hearing without authorization. The response is due within two business days in three pages, and a reply within one business day in two pages. Don’t spend space on background, make your arguments in the briefing, and don’t incorporate conferral letters or emails by reference. The judge may rule without a hearing. Disputed discovery motions that skip these steps are denied, though joint motions for stipulated orders are fine.

docs.t: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Panayotta Augustin-Birch, S.D. Fla.. Objections: Not reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence is outdated and meritless. Relevance and proportionality objections need a specific explanation. No boilerplate or general objections. Vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless, and burden needs an affidavit or similar statement. Seek clarification before objecting to vagueness and confer to narrow scope, then provide the undisputed discovery. An objection followed by an answer subject to or without waiving it preserves nothing. Privilege objections must follow Local Rule 26.1(e)(2), and a missing privilege log can waive the objection.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Scope: The judge’s procedures apply to all civil cases assigned or referred to the judge and take precedence over the local rules’ procedures under Local Rule 26.1(g)(1). If the district judge’s order conflicts, for example by barring discovery motions, and no order says how to submit a dispute, email chambers asking for instructions with the subject “Request re: Submission of Discovery Dispute in [Case Number]” and don’t describe the dispute.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Conferral: Counsel must actually speak, in person, by phone, or by Zoom. Email alone isn’t enough. Discuss options and make a concerted good-faith effort, and include a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate in the motion.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Discovery motion
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Discovery motion: File a discovery motion of no more than five pages that frames the issues, cites the best authority, and attaches the relevant requests and responses, described under CM/ECF procedure 3L(2). The response is due within five business days in five pages, and no reply is allowed. The judge then decides whether a hearing is needed.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — After a hearing is set
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. After a hearing is set: Keep trying to resolve it and email chambers promptly to cancel or narrow the hearing, copying all counsel and giving no argument or background in the email.

docs.t: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Eduardo I. Sanchez, S.D. Fla.. Objections: No boilerplate or general objections. Vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome alone is meaningless, and burden may need an affidavit. Ask for clarification before objecting to vagueness. Say whether a request is irrelevant or disproportionate and why. Confer to narrow scope, and produce the undisputed part. An objection followed by an answer subject to it preserves nothing. State that everything responsive has been produced or describe what you’re withholding. Privilege objections need the specifics and a log, or may be waived.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Motion for Discovery Hearing
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Motion for Discovery Hearing: After conferring under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3), file a “Motion for Discovery Hearing,” and no other discovery motion or memorandum without the judge’s permission. It may contain only: a short statement of the disputed issues and relief sought, a list of documents you’ll rely on at the hearing (not discovery materials), a list of legal authorities with a parenthetical for each and which issue it applies to but no argument, any time constraints, at least three Tuesday-through-Friday dates within 14 days when the parties are available (or simply say they couldn’t agree), any request to file a formal motion or memorandum, and a certificate of conferral. No exhibits or conferral emails. Noncompliant motions and responses may be stricken.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Response and email to chambers
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Response and email to chambers: The opposing party responds within three days with only the same items and no argument or exhibits, and no replies without leave. After filing, email the motion or response to the judge’s discovery address with the subject “Discovery Dispute” or “Response to Discovery Dispute,” the case number and name, and a one-sentence body in the judge’s form. Attach a proposed order (Word, 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, justified, page-numbered after page one) and highlighted source materials, attaching only the responses if they’ve been filed. Conferral emails aren’t source material.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Hearings
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Hearings: The judge sets hearings in person in Fort Lauderdale, and grants a Zoom request if the lawyer arguing is outside the district. A motion to continue needs three alternative Tuesday-through-Friday dates. To bring a laptop or other equipment, file a short motion at least 24 hours before saying who and what. Present exhibits by Zoom screen share. Judge Shaw-Wilder encourages less-experienced lawyers to argue.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Timing
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Timing: Raise disputes as Local Rule 26.1(g)(2) requires, and finish all discovery, including disputes, before the cutoff under Rule 26.1(d). The judge enforces both.

docs.t: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder (S.D. Fla.) — Other
docs.x: Judge Detra Shaw-Wilder, S.D. Fla.. Other: A stipulation isn’t a court order, so move for a Rule 26(c) protective order and email the Word version, and the judge omits any provision that would bypass Local Rule 5.4’s sealing rules. Seek sanctions by separate motion. A pending motion to stay discovery doesn’t excuse responding to discovery.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Chambers email
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Chambers email: The judge’s page gives one address for proposed orders, jury instructions and other filings the court directs, and a separate address for discovery matters under the judge’s procedures.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Conferral and timing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Conferral and timing: Confer in person, by video, or by phone, since email alone isn’t enough, and certify it under Local Rule 7.1(a)(3). The judge strictly enforces Local Rule 26.1(g)(2) and reads the 28-day window as the time to make good-faith resolution efforts, with the seven-day extension under 26.1(g)(2)(C) only, and won’t recognize extensions the parties agree to without approval. All discovery, including disputes, must be finished before the cutoff and no remedy is available after it.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — No discovery motions
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. No discovery motions: Don’t raise discovery disputes by Rule 37 motion without leave, because they’ll be stricken. The restriction doesn’t apply to motions to stay discovery or to extend the time to respond to discovery, which go to the district judge.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Setting a hearing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Setting a hearing: Email chambers within the Rule 26.1(g)(2) time, copying opposing counsel, with the subject “Request for Discovery Hearing on [Case Number and Case Name],” at least three dates in the next ten days showing morning, afternoon, or all-day availability, and no argument. The judge ordinarily allows 30 minutes per side, and you must state if you need more. The hearings aren’t informal, so be fully prepared.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Notice of Hearing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Notice of Hearing: Within one business day of the judge’s confirming the date, file a Notice of Hearing of no more than five pages per side outlining each issue and each side’s position, without argument. Attach a short proposed order, all relevant source materials, and a list of the legal authorities with copies (highlighting and parentheticals allowed but no argument), and include a Local Rule 7.1(a)(3) certificate. Nothing more can be submitted without leave. Don’t file conferral emails, which the judge doesn’t accept as evidence of conferral. Notify chambers and file a Notice of Cancellation if you resolve everything.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Agreed orders
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Agreed orders: Don’t move for an agreed order. Email chambers the proposed order in Word with a statement that the parties agree. The judge doesn’t enter stipulated orders extending the time to respond to discovery or memorializing discovery agreements that weren’t litigated.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Objections
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Objections: Blanket vague, overbroad, or unduly burdensome objections are meaningless, and you may need sworn evidence of burden. Seek clarification before objecting to vagueness. An objection followed by an answer subject to it preserves nothing, so say that everything responsive was provided or describe what is withheld. Privilege objections need the Local Rule 26.1(e)(2)(B) details and a log, and the party with the burden must file any sworn evidence as an exhibit to the Notice of Hearing or may waive the privilege. Produce the undisputed part when objecting on scope. Object to a Rule 30(b)(6) notice’s scope by serving, not filing, the objections before the deposition, and the judge decides them only after it.

docs.t: Judge Yeney Hernandez (S.D. Fla.) — Sequencing
docs.x: Judge Yeney Hernandez, S.D. Fla.. Sequencing: Each party may sequence its own discovery under Rule 26(d)(3), so one side’s discovery doesn’t make the other wait. Don’t leave depositions to the end, because failing to finish them before the cutoff isn’t good cause to extend it.

docs.t: Judge Gordon Gallagher (D. Colo.) — Where the judge sits
docs.x: Judge Gordon Gallagher, D. Colo.. Where the judge sits: Judge Gallagher sits in Grand Junction at the Wayne Aspinall Federal Building, courtroom 323, chambers 310, (970) 241-8932. The judge has no differences marked in the uniform standards.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Scope: Judges Rodriguez, Sweeney, Wang, Gallagher, and Crews share one set of Uniform Civil Practice Standards, effective December 9, 2025, with a judge’s initials marking any variation. Failing to follow them, the Local Rules, or the Federal Rules can get a filing struck without substantive consideration.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Extensions and continuances
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Extensions and continuances: Ask for an extension by written motion as far ahead as possible, showing particular good cause. The press of business typically isn’t good cause, and a motion filed after the original deadline won’t be considered. Note service on the client in the certificate of service, naming who received it. Ask for a continuance by written motion too. Oral motions on the day of a hearing or trial aren’t entertained, a stipulated continuance isn’t effective until the court approves it, and you should email chambers when you file.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Motions generally: Motion and argument go in one document, since a separately filed brief is noncompliant. Send a Word proposed order by email with any joint or unopposed motion. Exhibits are separate attachments labeled by number and name. Email chambers when you file an emergency motion. Separate requests for different actions need separate motions, and a request for action can’t be buried in a response or reply. Untimely or noncompliant papers may be denied or stricken on the court’s own motion. For Judge Rodriguez, supporting exhibits go in one consecutively numbered appendix, and a respondent adds its own.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Motions to dismiss and Rule 702
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Motions to dismiss and Rule 702: Each party gets one Rule 12(b) motion unless the court orders otherwise, and you must meet and confer first or it may be struck, except with unrepresented or incarcerated parties. Rule 702 motions are due 30 days after the rebuttal disclosure deadline, attach the report, list each opinion challenged, say whether you want a hearing, and cover all challenges in a single motion.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Summary judgment: One motion per party absent exceptional circumstances. Inside the brief, a numbered Statement of Undisputed Material Facts with record cites, a Response admitting or denying each paragraph, a Statement of Additional Disputed Facts, and Reply sections, with no legal argument in those sections. Judges Rodriguez, Sweeney, and Crews each have their own Standing Order on Rule 56 motions, which replaces or must be followed before this section, so read theirs.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Format and page limits
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Format and page limits: Double-spaced Arial 12-point (Judge Crews wants Century Schoolbook 12-point, with single-spaced 12-point footnotes). Bluebook citations with pinpoints, and Westlaw cites for unpublished cases (Crews accepts Lexis). Motions, responses, and briefs are 15 pages and replies 10. Summary judgment motions and responses are 20 pages and replies 10. Objections to a magistrate judge are 10 pages with no reply absent leave. Notices of supplemental authority can’t contain argument.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Settlement and discovery
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Settlement and discovery: File a settlement Status Report within 14 days after discovery closes. A request for a settlement conference needs a written demand and response first. Tell chambers by email of a settlement and file a Notice of Settlement, but dates aren’t vacated until dismissal papers are filed. In employment cases alleging adverse action filed after August 1, 2022, the Initial Discovery Protocols apply within 30 days after the response and replace initial disclosures.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Hearings and trial
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Hearings and trial: File a glossary five business days ahead and bring three paper copies. File a joint exhibit list and witness list two business days before any hearing, with three paper copies. Pre-mark exhibits and deliver bound, labeled notebooks to chambers by 9:00 a.m. two business days ahead. Judge Wang takes one original binder plus two thumb drives, and Judge Crews one binder plus a thumb drive, both to the clerk’s office. Ask for video testimony by motion or stipulation at least 7 days ahead. Each judge’s own Standing Order covers trial setting and trial procedures.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Chambers: Chambers can’t give legal advice or grant oral requests, so don’t call about substance. Email with the case name and number in the subject, copying all parties. Judge Crews takes only a joint email to the chambers address and doesn’t want calls or visits. Send proposed orders as Word attachments only when directed.

docs.t: Judge Kato Crews (D. Colo.) — Judge Crews’s own differences
docs.x: Judge Kato Crews, D. Colo.. Judge Crews’s own differences: Do not call or visit chambers: contact it only by a joint email. Use Century Schoolbook 12-point (footnotes 12-point, single-spaced). Lexis citations are fine for unpublished cases. Summary judgment follows the judge’s Standing Order Regarding Rule 56 Motions. Mark plaintiff’s exhibits with numbers and defendant’s with letters, with no duplicates, and deliver one binder plus a thumb drive to the clerk’s office two business days ahead.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Scope: Judge Brimmer’s Practice Standards (civil), effective December 1, 2025, apply alongside the Federal and Local Rules and the ECF procedures.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Chambers: Don’t contact the law clerks about procedural or scheduling matters. Send a proposed order by email only when chambers asks, as a Word attachment. Don’t submit proposed judgments, since the clerk prepares them. Proposed orders for motions go through CM/ECF.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Extensions and continuances
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Extensions and continuances: An extension needs particular good cause and must be filed no later than three business days before the due date. Agreement of counsel, inconvenience, the press of business, scheduling conflicts, or practicing as a sole practitioner aren’t good cause. Don’t ask for a continuance at the hearing or trial, and a stipulated continuance isn’t effective until the court approves it.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Settlement: Tell the judge’s judicial assistant as soon as possible. A hearing or bench trial is vacated only if pleadings that resolve the matter are filed by noon on the last business day before it, or else counsel appear to recite the terms. Jury costs can be assessed under D.C.COLO.LCivR 54.2 if a case settles after noon on the last business day before trial. Settlement talks don’t continue hearings, trials, or deadlines. The court generally won’t retain jurisdiction to enforce a settlement.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Discovery: Deadlines and limits are set by the assigned magistrate judge, and the presumptive discovery period is six months.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Motions: Motions, objections, responses, and briefs are 15 pages and replies 10, including the cover page, statement of facts, and everything but the certificate of service, in 12-point type with footnotes the same size. Summary judgment motions and responses are 20 pages. No surreply without leave, and a motion for leave attaches the proposed surreply. Noncompliant motions may be denied or stricken on the court’s own motion.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Motions to dismiss
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Motions to dismiss: Rule 12(b) motions are discouraged if an amendment can fix the defect, so confer first. Don’t plead a Rule 12(b) motion in the alternative as a Rule 56 motion. For each Rule 12(b)(6) claim, list each element you say wasn’t alleged, and the respondent marks each element “DISPUTED” and cites the page and paragraph where it’s pleaded.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Summary judgment: A numbered Statement of Undisputed Material Facts with specific record cites, a Response, optional Statements of Additional Disputed and Undisputed Facts, and Reply sections, with no legal argument in those sections. Failing to follow this can get the motion struck or facts deemed admitted.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Experts and trial
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Experts and trial: A motion to exclude opinion testimony names each opinion and ground, and the deadline is set at the scheduling conference, otherwise 30 days after rebuttal expert disclosures. Motions in limine are discouraged and are due 14 days before the Trial Preparation Conference, with responses at 7 days. At 14 days before it, file proposed jury instructions with sources, and email them in Word with a separate verdict form. At 7 days, file witness and exhibit lists and voir dire questions. The Trial Preparation Conference is usually about two weeks before trial, and trial counsel must attend in person.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Exhibits and depositions
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Exhibits and depositions: File a joint-style exhibit list on the court’s form two business days before a motion hearing. Plaintiff’s exhibits use yellow labels with numbers and defendant’s use blue labels with letters, bound in labeled notebooks, with separate sets for the court, deputy, reporter, law clerk, opposing counsel, and witness. Designate deposition testimony by page and line, with designations 60 days before trial and counter-designations at 45 days, objections within 14 days in a four-column table.

docs.t: Judge Philip A. Brimmer (D. Colo.) — Jury trials
docs.x: Judge Philip A. Brimmer, D. Colo.. Jury trials: Counsel appear at 8:00 a.m. on the first day and selection starts at 8:30. The jury is usually nine with three peremptory challenges per side and 15 minutes of voir dire per side after the court. Jurors may take notes and receive written instructions, and the jury is charged before closings. The court typically doesn’t sit on Fridays.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Communications
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Communications: Don’t call chambers. Email with the case number and name in the subject and copy all counsel. Chambers can’t give legal advice or grant informal requests not made by motion. Send proposed orders both through CM/ECF and by email in editable Word format, copying all counsel.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Length is by word count
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Length is by word count: Motions, objections, responses, and briefs are limited to 4,000 words, replies to 2,700, and summary judgment and preliminary injunction or restraining order papers to 5,500 words. Footnotes count, and the caption, tables, signature block, and certificates don’t. Every paper must end with a certification, right after the signature block, that it complies with the limit. A motion to exceed the limit is due three business days before the paper is due. Papers by parties without word processing get page limits instead (10, 15, and 20 pages).

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Format and citations
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Format and citations: Any proportionally spaced serif font. Bluebook or any consistent, clear citation form. Give Westlaw cites for unpublished opinions, or attach them. Mark exhibits by number and name, and don’t re-attach exhibits already filed with an earlier paper. No sur-reply or supplemental brief without leave. A notice of supplemental authority may give only the citation, its date, and a one-sentence statement of the issue.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Rule 12 and amendments
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Rule 12 and amendments: Rule 12 motions are discouraged where an amendment can cure the defect, and counsel must confer before any Rule 12(b), (c), (e), or (f) motion and describe the conferral efforts in the motion. Don’t plead a Rule 12(b)(6) or 12(c) motion as an alternative Rule 56 motion. The court freely grants a timely motion to amend, and futility arguments are better raised in a Rule 12 motion after the amended pleading is filed.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Summary judgment: A Statement of Undisputed Facts, a Response, a Statement of Additional Facts, and Reply sections, with no legal argument in them. You must admit or deny the factual substance, so you can’t deny based on inadmissibility (object concisely instead), can’t deny for lack of knowledge without a Rule 56(d) request and affidavit, and can’t say a document “speaks for itself.” Failing to follow this can get the motion struck.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Experts and emergencies
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Experts and emergencies: A motion to exclude an expert is due 30 days after rebuttal expert disclosures if the scheduling order has no date, and an issue not raised that way is waived or forfeited. Attach the expert’s full report. An emergency motion is only for imminent, irreparable harm: begin the caption with “Emergency,” use the CM/ECF Emergency event, and email chambers.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Settlement and continuances
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Settlement and continuances: File a notice of settlement stating how long you need for dismissal papers. On the eve of a hearing or trial, also email chambers with “Settlement” in the subject. Nothing is vacated until the court orders it, jury costs can be assessed under Local Civil Rule 54.2 for a settlement after noon on the last business day before a jury trial, and the court generally won’t retain jurisdiction over a settled case. Continuance motions made at the hearing or trial aren’t entertained, and a stipulated continuance isn’t effective until approved.

docs.t: Judge Daniel D. Domenico (D. Colo.) — Courtroom and trial
docs.x: Judge Daniel D. Domenico, D. Colo.. Courtroom and trial: File a glossary five business days before any hearing or trial. Agree on one exhibit numbering system from the start of discovery, use the same numbers for depositions and trial, and mark exhibits by number only. The court sets a Final Pretrial Conference about three to four weeks before trial and a Trial Preparation Conference the week before, and trial counsel must attend both. Make Batson challenges after peremptories end and before the jury is sworn, and ask that jurors not be released. Jurors may take notes and receive written instructions.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Scope and chambers
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Scope and chambers: The judge’s Revised Practice Standards (effective December 1, 2022) have the force of orders and add to the Local Rules. Don’t contact chambers about substance. Ex parte contact by letter or phone is barred, so everything goes in a motion, brief, notice, or status report served on all parties. The magistrate judge generally manages discovery and discovery disputes.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Extensions and trial continuances
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Extensions and trial continuances: Seek extensions or continuances by written motion with good cause as far ahead as possible. Absent a compelling reason, an extension motion must be filed by the original deadline and a hearing continuance by the court business day before the hearing. Trial continuances are heavily discouraged and will rarely be granted, and a conflicting trial before another court doesn’t count as substantial good cause.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Motions: One document for motion and argument, with exhibits filed the same day as separate attachments. A proposed order only if chambers asks. Every request for action must be in its own motion, and not in a brief, notice, or response. Tell the court if a motion becomes moot. Page limits are 15 for most motions and responses with 10 for replies, 10 for Rule 702 motions with a 5-page reply, 10 for Rule 72 objections and responses, and 30 pages with a 15-page reply for a traditional summary judgment motion. No sur-reply or supplemental brief without leave. Oral argument is at the judge’s sole discretion, with a preference when an attorney with eight years or less experience will argue.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Rule 12 and amendments
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Rule 12 and amendments: The judge views Rule 12 motions as overused. Counsel must confer first, even though the local rule says otherwise, and the motion must have a conspicuous statement of the efforts made, or the movant risks a personal fee award. Defending a Rule 12(b)(6) motion with facts outside the complaint violates the judge’s standards. All Rule 12 requests go in one motion that names the subsection. A motion to amend attaches a clean copy and a redline.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Summary judgment: Each party gets one summary judgment motion, plus one optional Early Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed within 30 days of the initial scheduling order. A Movant’s Statement of Material Facts, a Response to it, a Statement of Additional Disputed Facts, and Reply sections follow the same restrictions as other D. Colo. judges: no denial for inadmissibility, no denial for lack of knowledge without a Rule 56(d) request and affidavit, no “speaks for itself.”

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Motions in limine and experts
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Motions in limine and experts: Each side gets one motion in limine, 10 pages with a 5-page response and no reply, after conferral, filed no earlier than 70 days and no later than 21 days before the Final Trial Preparation Conference. A Rule 702 motion is due 70 days before that conference, or with the summary judgment response or reply if it targets summary judgment evidence, and must not be styled a motion in limine.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Pretrial: The magistrate judge holds the Final Pretrial Conference, and the judge holds a Final Trial Preparation Conference about two weeks before a civil trial, which trial counsel must attend in person or risk sanctions. Seven days before it, file the Final Witness List (listing will-call and may-call witnesses with time estimates), a Final List of Proposed Exhibits (no duplicates, with stipulations marked), proposed voir dire, and a list of open issues. Jury instructions, the statement of the case, and verdict forms are due 14 days before. Ask for a trial longer than five days within three days after the Final Pretrial Order.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Settlement: The judge won’t vacate the trial preparation conference or trial until you file a stipulation of dismissal or a stipulated notice of settlement saying all material terms are agreed. If court approval is needed, the judge won’t vacate until a motion for preliminary approval is filed. Within one week of scheduling a settlement conference or mediation, file a notice of it, and within three court days afterward file a notice of the outcome.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Trial and exhibits
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Trial and exhibits: Trial days start at 8:45 a.m. with counsel present at 8:30. Openings are 20 minutes per side, sidebars are discouraged, and leading questions on direct are readily sustained. Plaintiff’s exhibits are numbers and defendant’s are letters, with no duplicates, original binders for witnesses, copies for the court, and flash drives for the reporter. Designate depositions 21 days before trial, and file a joint marked transcript of objections seven days before. Don’t use deposition testimony of a witness who testifies live, except as the rules allow. Civil juries are eight with three peremptory strikes each, and Batson challenges come after strikes and before the jury is sworn.

docs.t: Judge William J. Martínez (D. Colo.) — Special matters
docs.x: Judge William J. Martínez, D. Colo.. Special matters: Don’t expect a TRO to issue ex parte except in strict compliance with Rule 65(b). A pending TRO or preliminary injunction motion refiled after removal will likely be stricken without prejudice. The Initial Discovery Protocols apply in employment cases alleging adverse action, within 30 days after the defendant’s first response.

docs.t: Judge Raymond P. Moore (D. Colo.) — Where they are
docs.x: Judge Raymond P. Moore, D. Colo.. Where they are: The judge posts civil Practice Standards, and the version we found is dated May 2013. They cover courtroom procedure, a required exhibit list and witness list form, and a Rule 56.1 summary judgment procedure. We haven’t read the details.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Scope: The judge’s Individual Rules and Practices (revised April 2020) control over any conflict with the Local Rules. Motions that don’t follow them are summarily denied. The motion rules don’t apply to Social Security appeals, habeas cases, bankruptcy appeals, pro se prisoner civil rights cases, or student loan cases.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Adjournments and extensions
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Adjournments and extensions: Ask in writing at least 48 hours before the date. State the original date, how many prior requests and how they were ruled on, and whether the other side consents and, if not, why. If other dates are affected, attach a proposed scheduling order that uses only business days.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Pre-motion letter and conference
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Pre-motion letter and conference: Before a motion to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, for summary judgment, for preliminary injunctive relief, or for sanctions, send a letter of no more than three double-spaced pages stating the grounds. The other side answers within three business days in three pages, describing its arguments and defenses. Don’t file the motion until the court enters an order on the letters. A Rule 12(b) letter stays the time to answer or move. Motions to dismiss are decided with prejudice unless the opposing party amended as of right before the motion or files, and the court grants, a cross-motion to amend.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Orders to show cause
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Orders to show cause: Any application by order to show cause needs a written explanation, with authority, of why ordinary motion practice isn’t available.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Briefs
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Briefs: Memoranda are up to 25 double-spaced pages and replies 10, with a table of contents and a table of authorities for any over 10 pages. One-inch margins and 12-point type for text and footnotes. Several parties on one side file jointly unless the court allows otherwise, and all opposing parties file one joint opposition, with any cross-motion inside it. One reply per motion, covering the cross-motion. No sur-reply without permission, requested by a one-page letter.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Filing
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Filing: Each exhibit is a separate docket attachment labeled with its number and a short description. Courtesy copies only when ordered, printed from CM/ECF, and bound, tabbed, and indexed. Most motions are decided on submission. Nothing may be filed under seal without prior authorization, with a declaration showing good cause and a proposed confidentiality order containing the language the judge specifies. A motion for default judgment needs a certificate of service showing it was served on the defaulting party.

docs.t: Judge Mae D’Agostino (N.D.N.Y.) — Removed cases
docs.x: Judge Mae D’Agostino, N.D.N.Y.. Removed cases: Within seven days after filing a notice of removal, file and serve a signed statement giving each defendant’s date of receiving and of service of the summons and complaint, New York citizenship for diversity cases (with each member’s citizenship for entities), reasons if removal came more than 30 days after the first receipt, and any served defendant who didn’t join and why.

docs.t: Judge Robert N. Chatigny (D. Conn.) — Dispositive motions
docs.x: Judge Robert N. Chatigny, D. Conn.. Dispositive motions: The judge requires a request for a pre-filing conference before any motion to dismiss or for summary judgment. For a motion to dismiss, ask as soon as possible after service of the summons and complaint. For summary judgment, ask usually no later than 45 days before the discovery deadline in the case management plan.
